An integer midpoint forces equal endpoint parities. At fixed normal the two marginals of each parity class have equal mass. Every product pair within that class has its integer base midpoint in P by lattice completeness. Compatibility supplies the full product midpoint inclusion into K_p.

With two nonempty sides the complete bipartite comparison against M_zw aligns all positive input affine face directions in that class. The affine offsets b_z are perpendicular to V, and u is also perpendicular to V. The physical height on the output level is consequently (h_z+h_w)/2, with no dependence on its continuous coordinate. By compatibility it is at most h_{K_p}.

A tight producing pair satisfies the ball and face-inclusion hypotheses for the actual K_p, so its target conditional is positive and its affine hull equals the averaged endpoint affine hull. Every other producing pair at the same auxiliary level is tight. This gives a single reachable tight offset over each physical p and a common actual target ceiling there. Off contact a finite sum of pair-average upper densities has finite integral and supplies every required product inequality.

For m=0 the conditional faces are singletons. The ball inequality on endpoint-centered small balls gives actual tight target atom mass at least the smaller input mass. Off contact the maximum of the finitely many minimum input ceilings satisfies the finite atom hypothesis. For d=1, counting measure on normals makes each original conditional atom unit mass, and the same finite selection and roof argument applies.

The orthogonal coordinate identification preserves intrinsic Lebesgue measure and convex order in the full physical coordinates. The roof test removes all below-contact levels. Domination by the actual target conditional survives the physical selector, and any feasible coupling's contribution at p needs a positive endpoint base pair whose heights add to 2h_{K_p}. The count is Borel by finite support and Borel kernels and is bounded by the number 2^n of parity classes.

In the sharpness example, for each coordinate the only even-sum pair from {0,1} × {1,2} is a complementary pair with sum two. All midpoint base mass is forced onto the all-ones site, while there are exactly 2^n original full boundary copies. Pairing complementary sites and identical boundary points gives an admissible law, also in n=0 and d=1.

issues.defect: If domination denotes measure inequality, as for the preceding kernel bounds, it fails for repeated body labels. For a single sampled site z=w=p, the tight triple has λ=3S_{K_z}, while the common reference is σ=S_{K_z}+S_{M_zz}=2S_{K_z}.
issues.locator: Proof paragraph 2, “Each triple's normal reference λ is dominated by σ”
issues.repair: Write explicitly that λ is absolutely continuous with respect to σ. Each constituent is absolutely continuous with respect to σ, and the remainder of the paragraph only needs this weaker comparison.

overlap.comparison: This gives factor-one actual middle-fiber surface repair for fixed endpoint sites −1 and 1 in a normal-preserving martingale, with source-row reconstruction. It does not handle arbitrary parity classes, competing output offsets, pair reassignment across a lattice-complete family, or the sharp uniform count.

Its parity midpoint construction uses independently paired full fiber-volume measures and controls base masses and halfspaces. It has no marked surface measures, exact target normal contact, or convex-order repair of a prescribed coupling.

initial_review.readability: After the roof step the actual target is an upper bound on the whole support graph. A ceiling restricted to the compact reachable output sets can agree with the target only on contributing tight levels and their reachable sets. Replacing “is exactly” by “is bounded by” there would avoid reading it as equality over unreachable sites.
